text: Sell SGLP.L now — it's nearly 100% off its 52-week high with rock-bottom relative strength, meaning this position is essentially broken and there's no reason to hold on hoping for a recovery.
Trim RGTI because you're down 27% in a stock with shrinking revenue, deep losses, and 15% short interest — this is the weakest holding in your portfolio and the thesis isn't working.

Trim QBTS since it's deeply unprofitable with repeated earnings misses and 15.5% short interest, meaning a lot of professional money is betting against it — reduce your exposure before the crowd gets louder.
Trim LASR to lock in some of that 69% gain — with a PE of 111, tiny free cash flow, and only £240 in the position, it makes sense to take profits on a stock this speculative.
Add to NVDA — a PE of 17 with 65% revenue growth makes this arguably the best value in your portfolio, and the AI chip leader deserves a larger position at these prices.
Add to META — at a PE of just 17 with 22% revenue growth and a consistent earnings beat streak, it's one of the cheapest big tech names you can own right now.
Add to MSFT while it's down 12% — a PE of 22 for a company growing revenue 15% with strong free cash flow is a rare discount on one of the highest-quality businesses in the world.
Add to LMT — a PE of 16 with nearly 6% free cash flow yield makes Lockheed Martin attractively valued as a steady defense blue chip in an uncertain world.
